headline: Brent crude falls below $98 after steepest weekly drop since April 2020 (>16% last week) as Trump says fresh Iran strikes 'highly'

sources: Reuters wire (oil prices) + Donald Trump phone interview with CNN (Nov 8)
fault_line: Is the war really over and prices safe -- or is this a trap before the next strike? (Social threads argue pump-price reality vs barrel price, and whether the drop is a real de-escalation signal or pre-strike calm.)

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT] Brent crude fell below $98 a barrel in early Asian trade Monday Nov 9 (CNBC TV18: $97.97; Al Jazeera liveblog 00:30 GMT citing Reuters: $97.67, down >0.5%; WTI $90.51), after losing more than 16% last week -- the steepest weekly drop since April 2020 -- retreating from a six-month high at end-October. Driver: traders betting the US-Iran conflict will not escalate after the Democrats' midterm sweep, plus Trump's CNN interview Nov 8 saying fresh strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress ('It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement'). Counter-pressure the same morning: Rubio said there is 'no progress' and Iran's demands are 'unacceptable'/'outrageous'; both sides reported shipping hit in/near Hormuz over the weekend (UKMTO: unknown projectile hit a tanker exiting Hormuz; Aramco offices damaged in Riyadh).
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: Reuters T1, Al Jazeera T2 (STATE QA), NDTV T3. Attribution-only (NOT counted, no declared tier): CNBC TV18, Economic Times, Deccan Chronicle, Business Today.
sections.what_disputed: Rubio (00:15 GMT, Homestead AFB) contradicts the de-escalation read: 'no progress', Iranian demands 'unacceptable' and 'outrageous'; physical supply risk unchanged -- Hormuz transits collapsed (see hidden_constraint, STALE PortWatch) and Khor Mor gas field is out (2,800 MW, 03:00 item). TIMESTAMP NOTE: some indexed versions of the Reuters wire cite prices 'by 1134 GMT' -- that stamp post-dates this scan (02:00 UTC) and is NOT relied on; this record cites the AJ 00:30 GMT update and the CNBC TV18 05:01 piece only.
sections.why_matters: Oil crashed 16% in a week -- traders bet the war is over. The strait says otherwise. Pocketbook-first energy angle (Tier 1 demand) + reveal frame: price bets de-escalation while Hormuz transits sit at ~5% of baseline and Rubio says no progress.

totw_analysis: Our read: Oil crashed 16% in a week -- traders bet the war is over. The strait says otherwise. Pocketbook-first energy angle (Tier 1 demand) + reveal frame: price bets de-escalation while Hormuz transits sit at ~5% of baseline and Rubio says no progress. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the war really over and prices safe -- or is this a trap before the next strike?
